# borch

> PyTorch's shape in a browser tab. Three implementations of one API — a numpy core (`import borch as torch`), a TypeScript runtime on WebGPU (`borch-ts`), and a Python binding over it for Pyodide (`borch_webgpu`) — held to real PyTorch's values, error messages and printed form on thousands of golden cases. Nothing to install in the browser; `pip install pyborch` or `npm install borch-ts` elsewhere.

Pick by where the code runs: Python on a machine → `borch`; Pyodide/JupyterLite with WebGPU → `borch_webgpu`; a TypeScript page → `borch-ts`. CUDA, mixed precision, distributed training and `torch.compile` are absent by design and refused loudly. Check a name in `api-index.json` before writing it.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/AGENTS.md): the one page a coding agent needs — which of the three to use, ten rules that save a rewrite, three smoke tests, where the truth is
- [README](https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/README.md): the door — thirty seconds in Python and in TypeScript, where it runs, how it is guaranteed

## The long document

- [docs/BOOK.md](https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/docs/BOOK.md): installing and naming, the design principle, how the values are guaranteed, the supported range, borch.ts and its six differences from torch, the binding, the `cpu` device, what is deliberately not supported, conformance
- [BORCH-TS.md](https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/BORCH-TS.md): the TypeScript runtime on its own
- [ROADMAP.md](https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/ROADMAP.md): what conformance means here, and what will not be done

## Reference

- [api-index.json](https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/site/assets/api-index.json): every public name to its module — the quick "does this exist" check

- [API reference](https://playidea-lab.github.io/borch/site/api/): the same, browsable
